transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-17 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Rivera (Redwood SE), Priya Anand (Redwood SE), Dr. Lina Cho (Cascade Head of ML), Evan Brooks (Cascade Platform), Sana Iqbal (Cascade Security), Tom Hale (Cascade CTO)

[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick intro I'm Maya AE on the Redwood team, Diego and Priya from SEs are here to dig into the technical scope. how's everyone doing?
[00:10] Tom Hale: good, thanks Maya. we wanted to scope a POC to validate open models for RAG over our internal protocols and clinical docs, main concerns are accuracy and PHI handling.
[00:25] Dr. Lina Cho: yes, accuracy on Q/A over our annotated dossiers is the top metric, also throughput since we'll have spikey loads during analysis runs.
[00:35] Diego Rivera: great, can you walk us through current stack and what success looks like?
[00:40] Evan Brooks: sure, infra is GCP, k8s cluster, internal vector DB (we use Milvus), average payload is ~1.2k tokens per request after retrieval, expected steady QPS ~5 r/s with spikes to 25 for batch runs. latency target for interactive users is p95 < 1.2s for generation excluding retrieval.
[01:05] Priya Anand: ok that helps. do you need context windows beyond 8k? you mentioned long docs.
[01:12] Dr. Lina Cho: ideally support 32k for long consultation transcripts, but our first POC can focus on 8k to keep cost manageable. for medical accuracy we'll run a custom evaluation set.
[01:25] Maya Patel: perfect. success criteria from Redwood perspective we usually align around three pillars — quality (measured vs your eval set), latency/cost (tokens per second and $/1k tokens), and reliability (SLOs for p95/p99). what are your primary blockers?
[01:40] Sana Iqbal: security — we need to know data residency, whether model weights leave VPC during benchmark, KMS integration, audit logs, and SOC2 attestations. also questions about fine-tuning vs instruct-tuning open models.
[02:05] Diego Rivera: noted. for the POC we'll propose two deployment options: hosted Redwood with private VPC peering + customer-managed KMS, or Private deployment in your VPC for full isolation. benchmarking plan will include both latency and cost numbers for hosted vs private.
[02:25] Dr. Lina Cho: good. on models, we're focused on open families — what's your current shortlist?
[02:30] Maya Patel: from our experience and given biotech needs, we typically recommend a mix: Llama-2-13B-chat (quantized), Mistral-Instruct 8x, MPT-30B-Instruct, and Falcon-40B-instruct. we also sometimes evaluate Mosaic MPT-7B-Instruct and specialist fine-tuned L2 variants. each has tradeoffs: model size vs latency/cost vs instruction-following and domain robustness.
[02:58] Dr. Lina Cho: any thoughts on medical domain robustness out of the box?
[03:05] Diego Rivera: open models vary — larger models like 30-40B tend to be better at nuanced Q/A but cost more and need more memory. some companies have fine-tuned Llama-2 variants for biomedical text, that helps. we recommend starting with 13B Llama2 for baseline, plus one 30B-class for quality comparison.
[03:25] Evan Brooks: what's the expected cost delta between 13B and 30B at our load?
[03:30] Priya Anand: rough ballpark — at our QPS the per-token throughput and GPU utilization matter; a 13B quantized on A10/A100-nv4 (or equivalent) will be ~3-4x cheaper per token than a 30B on the same hardware, but the 30B may reduce error rates on complex queries. we'll provide cost estimates in the spreadsheet.
[03:55] Tom Hale: we have multilingual needs — French and German collaborators in EU, any of these models handle multilingual biomedical text well?
[04:05] Diego Rivera: Llama-2 shows some multilingual capability; Mistral and Falcon too, but domain-specific performance varies. if multilingual accuracy is critical, we can include a translation+monolingual pipeline in the POC or evaluate a multilingual fine-tuned variant.
[04:25] Sana Iqbal: regarding PHI, will the models be allowed to see raw PHI during evaluation? we prefer masked or synthetic data for benching.
[04:33] Maya Patel: agreed, we recommend synthetic or de-identified samples for open model benching; for private deployment we can run on real deid data inside your VPC with no egress. action item: Evan to share sample prompts and a redacted dataset.
[04:50] Dr. Lina Cho: timeline — we were hoping to run something in 4 weeks, is that realistic?
[04:55] Maya Patel: yes, typical POC timeline: week 0-1 finalize scope and data sharing, week 2-3 run benchmarks across 2-3 models and deployment options, week 4 review results and recommend next steps. if you want extended can go to 6 weeks to include fine-tuning.
[05:15] Diego Rivera: benchmark metrics we'll collect: EM/accuracy on your eval set, latency p50/p95/p99, GPU utilization, tokens/sec, and per-1k-token cost. also memory footprint and cold-start times for KV cache.
[05:30] Evan Brooks: what's KV cache? we've seen references in your docs.
[05:33] Diego Rivera: sorry that's KV cache — the key-value cache that stores past token activations to speed up autoregressive decoding. it's important for long-context efficiency. sometimes transcribed as K V cash by STT :), so note.
[05:50] Priya Anand: for our benchmarking we'll include retrieval latency + model generation latency to give end-to-end numbers. also include streaming vs non-streaming cost differences.
[06:05] Tom Hale: can Redwood help with quantization guidance? we might prefer 4-bit quantized models to reduce footprint.
[06:12] Maya Patel: yes, Redwood Optimize includes quantization recommendations and we can run MQA-style or GPTQ pipelines for the POC. we'll note any quality regressions.
[06:25] Dr. Lina Cho: if we want to consider fine-tuning on our corpora later, what's the path?
[06:30] Diego Rivera: two options: instruction-tuning with adapter layers (cheap) or LoRA-style adapters for parameter-efficient fine-tuning. both can be tested in phase 2; phase 1 is zero-shot/instruct evals.
[06:45] Evan Brooks: for the hosted option, what guarantees do you provide for audit logs and retention?
[06:50] Maya Patel: hosted can be configured with tenant-level audit logs and export to your SIEM; retention is configurable as an add-on. Private deployment gives you full control and local storage. we'll include SOC2 and KMS notes in the security pack.
[07:05] Sana Iqbal: do you support customer-managed KMS/HSM for encrypting model keys?
[07:08] Priya Anand: yes, for Private deployment we integrate with your KMS and HSMs; for hosted we support CMEK options and customer-managed keys in supported clouds.
[07:25] Dr. Lina Cho: benchmark specifics — we plan 200 dev prompts and 1k eval prompts with a mix of short Q/A and long-document synthesis. can Redwood run the RAG pipeline end-to-end?
[07:36] Diego Rivera: yes, we can run retrieval + reranking + generation and provide per-stage timings. we recommend you supply the vector DB snapshot or allow read-only access for consistent runs.
[07:50] Evan Brooks: on vector DB we prefer to run against a snapshot export; we'll supply that.
[07:55] Maya Patel: perfect. on models we'll propose testing: Llama-2-13B-chat (quantized), Mistral-Instruct-8x, MPT-30B-Instruct (float/quant), and Falcon-40B-Instruct if memory allows. plus a smaller MPT-7B as a cost baseline. that gives a spectrum of cost vs quality.
[08:20] Dr. Lina Cho: do you have prior biotech benchmarks we can reference?
[08:25] Maya Patel: we have anonymized case studies and a public benchmark deck — will share links. note that proper domain benching requires your prompts and docs.
[08:35] Tom Hale: any red flags for on-prem hardware? our on-prem GPUs are primarily A100 40GB and some L40s.
[08:43] Diego Rivera: A100 40GB is ideal for 30-40B models with some sharding; L40s are okay for 13B-30B quantized. we'll include recommended instance shapes and memory configs in the runbook.
[09:00] Priya Anand: operationally we'll measure cold-starts, model load times, and how steady-state batching affects latency. also will test with prefix caching for repeated queries.
[09:12] Dr. Lina Cho: how will you present results?
[09:15] Maya Patel: we'll deliver a spreadsheet with per-model metrics, unit economics (cost per 1k tokens), recommendation matrix mapping to your success criteria, and a short exec slide deck.
[09:28] Evan Brooks: fine. any compliance constraints for the hosted option regarding EU data residency?
[09:33] Sana Iqbal: yes, data for EU collaborators must stay in EU region; can Redwood pin regions for hosted?
[09:38] Maya Patel: yes, we can route and pin requests to specific regions and run models in EU datacenters for residency. for full compliance we recommend Private deployment.
[09:50] Dr. Lina Cho: sample success criteria to confirm: 1) EM on eval >= baseline threshold (we define), 2) p95 generation latency <1.2s for interactive flows, 3) per-1k-token cost under target TBD, 4) security checklist satisfied.
[10:05] Tom Hale: agreed. let's capture those as the POC success criteria.
[10:12] Maya Patel: noted. next steps: we'll send model shortlist + perf/cost estimate by Friday, Diego will draft benchmark runbook, Evan to share prompts and snapshot, Sana to share SOC2 scope questions. schedule technical benchmark run during week of 2026-03-02.
[10:30] Dr. Lina Cho: one smaller question — hallucinations on long context, any mitigations?
[10:35] Diego Rivera: yes, we track hallucination rates via precision-focused evals and use grounding strategies: higher retrieval top-k, reranker, and conservative decoding settings. quantized models can slightly increase hallucinations so we'll flag that.
[10:50] Priya Anand: also will instrument model confidence scoring and include human-in-loop fallback thresholds for sensitive outputs.
[11:02] Maya Patel: great, thank you all. we'll follow up with the docs and schedule.
[11:08] Tom Hale: thanks everyone, looking forward.

End transcript.
